name: mid-backend-python-verbose
note: A rambling, paragraph-heavy resume in UK spelling with buried achievements and no consistent bullet structure. Five years Python backend against a Django platform role. Partial: the Python and Postgres are strong, the posting wants Celery at scale and AWS depth she only touches. Tests whether the rewrite can find the signal in prose rather than only reformatting bullets.
resume_text:
Aishwarya Menon
Senior Software Engineer (Backend) - Kochi, Kerala, India - working remotely since 2021
aishwarya.menon@example.com - +91 48423 66710 - linkedin.com/in/aishwaryamenon

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY

I have been writing backend software professionally for a little over five years, almost
all of it in Python, and almost all of it on systems that other teams depend on rather than
products that end users see directly. I like the work where the requirements are genuinely
ambiguous and somebody has to go and find out what the business actually needs before any
code gets written, and I have ended up doing quite a lot of that. I am comfortable being
the person who says the deadline is wrong.

EMPLOYMENT HISTORY

Merideon Systems (remote, company based in Bengaluru)
Senior Software Engineer, January 2023 to present, promoted from Software Engineer in
July 2024

Merideon sells a compliance reporting platform to banks and insurers. I work on the data
ingestion side of it, which is the part that takes regulatory filings in whatever shape the
customer's source system produces them and turns them into something the reporting engine
can use. When I joined there were three ingestion paths written by three different people
at three different times and none of them shared any code, so my first six months were
largely spent consolidating those into one pipeline with pluggable parsers, which was
tedious but has meant that adding a new customer format is now a matter of writing one
parser class and a test fixture rather than a fortnight of work. I wrote most of that
pipeline in Python with Pydantic for validation and it processes somewhere in the region of
two hundred thousand filings a month at the moment, though the number moves about depending
on the regulatory calendar. I also rewrote the reconciliation job, which had been a single
enormous function, into a set of smaller steps that could be retried independently, and
this mattered because previously a failure at the last stage meant redoing four hours of
work. I look after the Postgres side of things as well, including a fairly involved
partitioning change we made last year to keep query times reasonable as the filings table
grew past a hundred million rows. I mentor two juniors, I run our fortnightly design review,
and I am the person the support team escalates to when an ingestion run has gone wrong,
which happens less often now than it used to.

Calloway Analytics, Kochi
Software Engineer, August 2020 to December 2022

This was a smaller company, about thirty people. I worked on internal APIs in Django and
Django REST Framework for a marketing analytics product. I built the reporting API that the
front-end consumed, added caching with Redis when the dashboard load became a problem, and
wrote a lot of Celery tasks for the nightly aggregation runs. I also spent an unglamorous
but useful six months improving the test suite, which had been slow and flaky enough that
people had stopped trusting it; getting it from around eighteen minutes to under five and
removing the intermittent failures probably did more for the team's velocity than any
feature I shipped there. Towards the end I was involved in the move from a single EC2 box
to a containerised setup, though I was not the person leading that work.

EDUCATION

B.Tech in Computer Science and Engineering, Cochin University of Science and Technology,
2016 to 2020.

TECHNICAL SKILLS

Python (five years, primary language), Django, Django REST Framework, FastAPI, Pydantic,
SQLAlchemy, PostgreSQL including partitioning and query optimisation, Redis, Celery,
RabbitMQ, pytest, Docker, Git, GitLab CI, some AWS (EC2, S3, RDS), Linux.
jd_text:
Senior Backend Engineer (Python/Django)
Remote, India | Platform Team

Our platform serves logistics operators across South and Southeast Asia. The backend is a
Django monolith of significant age with three extracted services around it, all Python. We
are not going to tell you it is beautiful. It is well tested, it is understood, and it makes
money, and we are improving it in the places that hurt rather than rewriting it.

The platform team is six engineers and owns the core domain: shipments, consignments,
pricing and the integration layer with customer ERPs.

Responsibilities
- Design and build backend features in Django and Django REST Framework
- Own the asynchronous processing layer. We run a large Celery estate against RabbitMQ and
  it needs someone who understands queue routing, idempotency and what happens when a task
  is retried after a partial write
- Work on PostgreSQL performance at a scale where query plans matter: our largest tables are
  in the hundreds of millions of rows and partitioned
- Build and maintain customer integrations, which are almost never as documented as the
  customer believes
- Improve the deployment story with the infrastructure team. We are on AWS with ECS and
  Terraform
- Mentor. Two of the six are in their first two years and deserve better than to be left
  alone with the codebase

Requirements
- 5+ years of backend engineering, with at least 3 in Python
- Django and Django REST Framework in production, including the ORM at the level where you
  know what query it is about to run
- Celery at real volume, and the operational scars that come with it
- PostgreSQL: indexing, explain plans, migrations against large tables, and ideally
  partitioning
- Redis for caching and for the things people misuse Redis for
- Testing discipline. We will ask you about a test suite you made better
- Clear written communication. The team is fully remote across three cities

Desirable
- AWS at depth: ECS, RDS, SQS, IAM, and enough to debug your own infrastructure
- Terraform
- FastAPI, for the newer extracted services
- Event-driven architecture and message broker design
- Experience with regulated or compliance-heavy domains
- Having led a migration or consolidation of duplicated systems, and lived with the result

Compensation 32 to 45 LPA. Fully remote within India, one week together in Bengaluru each
quarter, travel paid.
